flags.title: Four editions of this publication are published under one domain; only the root one is in the sitemap
flags.detail: This repository publishes four separate reader-facing editions under the same domain and the same tracking ID: the root publication (ShopNow Kitchen), /editorial/, /counter/ (Crisp & Counter), /counterwise/ and /crisp-index/, with frozen earlier editions under /legacy/. Only the root publication is listed in sitemap.xml; the others are excluded from the index through robots.txt and noindex metadata, and they are all reachable from the single archive page. Google states that scaled content abuse includes "pages without unique content or purpose" and site reputation abuse covers "many low-quality pages"; several near-identical editions of the same five products on one domain is the pattern those policies describe. The root publication is the one that is indexed, and the others are preserved rather than deleted, so the owner can publish any of them on its own domain later if that is preferred.
flags.impact: Five near-identical editions on one domain split the search signals and the tracking data. The fix applied here is one indexed site plus a labelled archive; the owner can reverse it for any edition.
flags.manual_step: Decide which single edition is the product, and whether the other three should stay on this domain at all. Suggestion S-11 records the options; each edition keeps its own generator and gate, so republishing one is a one-line change.

flags.title: The tracking ID's shape does not match the example format in the policy, which is not the same as being wrong
flags.detail: Participation Requirements §2(b) gives the tag format as "XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate". The supplied ID shopnow047c-20 has an eleven-character prefix rather than five, and a two-digit suffix that does match. Because the clause expressly allows other designated formats, the shape proves nothing either way: it cannot confirm the ID is valid and it cannot show it is invalid. Recorded so nobody later reads the eleven-character prefix as evidence of a problem, and so the weaker argument - an Associates help page saying IDs end in -20 - is not mistaken for the policy text. Separately §1(g) bars any Amazon trademark or variant in a tag or Associates ID; shopnow047c contains none, which is a genuine pass.
flags.impact: None on its own. It narrows what may be concluded from the ID's appearance and leaves ownership unconfirmed.
flags.manual_step: Export the tracking-ID list from Associates Central and confirm shopnow047c-20 appears on it; that closes this flag and FLG-011 together.

flags.title: The published site carried no privacy notice while loading a click counter on every page
flags.detail: Participation Requirements §3(e) makes the Associate responsible for disclosing "either through a privacy policy or otherwise, the use of cookies, pixels, and other technologies by you and third parties and how you collect, use, store, and disclose data collected from visitors". For most of this repository's history the site loaded assets/analytics.js on every page with no notice anywhere on the live surface; privacy pages existed only under legacy/, belonging to superseded editions.
flags.impact: A disclosure obligation under the Associates policies that was unmet, and a reader-facing gap: nobody could tell what a page they were reading was doing.
flags.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-11-20 by main, independently of this session: a /privacy/ page now ships and states that nothing is collected while the endpoint is unset. This session's separately written draft was dropped in the merge rather than kept as a second privacy page. What remains open is Q-16: whether the shipped wording is adequate where the site is operated from, which is a question for the owner or counsel rather than a build session.
flags.manual_step: Review the shipped /privacy/ page against §3(e) and decide whether counsel should read it before any endpoint is configured (Q-16).

flags.title: Crawl control at a project path: robots.txt is not read from /Affil3/, and the other editions are not all noindexed
flags.detail: The root publication is served at https://karagemop466-tech.github.io/Affil3/. Search engines read robots.txt only from the host root (S25). The file generated by tools/build.mjs sits at /Affil3/robots.txt, so its Disallow lines for /editorial/, /legacy/ and /crisp-index/, and its Sitemap line, are not read from that path. https://karagemop466-tech.github.io/robots.txt returned an error on fetch. Only /editorial/ carries noindex on every page (21 of 21 html files). /counter/ has 0 of 23 files with noindex, /counterwise/ has 1 of 30, /crisp-index/ has 1 of 18, and /legacy/ has 4 of 100. The /docs/ publication named in the README is not in the working tree. A further edition, /counter-desk/, was merged to main after this branch was cut (commit 627ddfb). It has 32 html files, one of which carries noindex, its own sitemap and robots file, and it is not linked from the root publication or listed in the root sitemap. Rewriting robots.txt in this pass was not done, because it would look like a control without being one.
flags.impact: Near-duplicate copies of the same guides can compete with the root publication in search results. The sitemap is not discovered at the project path, so it must be submitted by hand.

flags.title: The CHEF iQ Sense specification table showed the ambient sensor range as the probe's temperature
flags.detail: The CHEF iQ specification page (S14) publishes two ranges: 'Internal temp range of 32ºF to 212ºF' and 'Ambient temp range of 32ºF to 1,000ºF'. The brand's own FAQ (S15) repeats the distinction: 'The max temperature for the portion of the probe inserted into the food is 212˚F... iQ Sense® Gen 3's maximum ambient temperature limit is 1,000ºF.' The register carried 32-1000 °F in temp_min_f/temp_max_f, so the product page and the side-by-side comparison table both rendered the ambient range as though it were the probe's food-temperature range. Corrected on 2026-11-20 to 32-212 °F, with the 1,000 °F ambient rating moved into the product's summary line, because a 1,000 °F figure sitting in a specification row invites the reading that the probe may be left in a 1,000 °F oven. The correction is recorded in the P05 record and in data/observations/2026-11-20-0e102530-verification.json.
flags.impact: A reader could reasonably have concluded the probe may be left in a 1,000 °F oven. The distinction between a sensor's surroundings and a probe's working limit is the difference between a safe instruction and a dangerous one. Both the product page and the comparison table now show the food range.
flags.action: Published 32-212 °F as the probe's food range and stated the 1,000 °F ambient rating separately in the summary line. Recorded as K-22 and opened as Q-20 with discovery step D-16.
flags.manual_step: Ask CHEF iQ in writing which range applies to which part of the probe in each cooking method, and publish the answer as a line of guidance beside the table rather than leaving a reader to infer it from two numbers.

flags.title: Two manufacturer pages disagree with themselves, and the site publishes no figure where that happens
flags.detail: The Emeril Lagasse page (S13) shows '25 Cooking Pre-sets' in its specification block, describes the appliance as '10-in-1' in its own product description, and carries an image whose alt text on the same page reads '11-in-1'. The Amazon listing title for the same product says '24 One-Touch Preset Options'. Separately, the CHEF iQ page (S14) says 'Five internal sensors' in its introduction while its specification list enumerates '4 internal temperature sensors' plus '1 ambient temperature sensor' - five in total, but not five internal ones. In both cases the site publishes no count: no preset count and no in-1 count for the oven, and the sensor count only as the specification list states it. Choosing between four official statements would be inference rather than verification.
flags.impact: Two of the products a reader is most likely to compare on features are the two whose feature counts cannot be published. The blank cells are correct and explained on each product page, but they make the comparison table less useful than a reader might expect.
flags.action: Published no preset count and no in-1 count for the Emeril oven, and followed the CHEF iQ specification list rather than its introduction. Both readings are kept dated rather than resolved by preference.
flags.manual_step: Ask each manufacturer which figure is current. Until then, treat any preset or in-1 count in a listing title as a claim, not a specification.

flags.title: Same-day short-link observations conflict: some rounds show product pages, others the Amazon home page
flags.detail: FLG-032 states that the other editions are 'excluded from the index through robots.txt and noindex metadata'. Checked against the tree on 2026-11-20: /editorial/ carries noindex, /crisp-index/ and /legacy/ were disallowed, and /counter/ and /counterwise/ were neither, although both ship an index.html, a sitemap.xml and a feed.xml of their own under the same domain. The frozen editions were not edited, in keeping with the archive rule that a preserved edition is not corrected; the fix is made where this build has authority. robots.txt is now generated from the repository: every root directory that publishes a page of its own, and every root-level markdown file, is excluded automatically, and tools/verify.mjs fails if the file falls behind the tree. The site-wide footer link into /editorial/ was removed, since a link from 43 pages is the crawl path a crawler follows. Stated limit, consistent with FLG-038: Google reads robots.txt only from the host root (S25), so on a project-path deploy these lines document intent rather than bind a crawler, and a disallowed page with no noindex tag can still be indexed by URL. The remaining half of the job is S-20 option B or C, which edits those editions and so belongs to whoever owns them.
flags.impact: No short link can be treated as confirmed for any product. The owner's own signed-in check and the G-02 test are the only way to settle it.
flags.manual_step: Decide S-20. Until then the live editions under counter/, counterwise/, crisp-index/ and editorial/ need a noindex meta tag on their own pages, which is a request in COORDINATION.md rather than an edit made here.
